docs/investigations/motor-subsystem-unlock.md:55-70 describes exactly this function's mechanics: comma-terminated per-channel MC/MC4 fields parsed off the shared packet buffer with cursor 0x20001fd4 (0x7a98's own sole RAM read/write) via FUN_0000799c (0x7a98's own callee 0x799c), where fields 1 and 3 are consumed by 'FUN_00007514/FUN_00007770 (display/status)' -- 0x7514 is likewise a direct callee of 0x7a98. docs/investigations/boot-and-hardware-bringup.md:301-307 independently identifies FUN_00007514 as the LCD status-line refresh, dispatching through a vtable-shaped indirect call into an Adafruit_GFX-style display-driver library. The 'DRIVER: ' string is therefore the LCD status-line label text drawn by that display call after per-channel MC4 config parsing -- fully consistent with, not competing against, the provenance_csv role ('MC/MC4 per-channel config parser + LCD status refresh caller'); the earlier 'ambiguous' string flag is resolved.

Level 1 (canonical docs) and Level 2 (in-packet RAM/caller cross-reference against the other 94 residual functions) found no specific match for 0xd1b4 or its RAM addresses (0x2000021c/0x20000220/0x200052f1) -- boot-and-hardware-bringup.md's ADC0/ADC1/DAC mention is the generic one-time boot clock-enable (FUN_0000cdd8), a different function. A bounded Level-3 decompile of 0xd1b4 itself (no caller-edge needed) shows the canonical ArduinoCore-samd wiring_analog.c analogRead(pin) idiom: pin-index remap (6->0x14, 7->0x15, <6 -> +0xe) matching g_APinDescription-style lookup; a guarded DAC-disable block (SYNCBUSY polling, ENABLE-bit clear) that only fires for the two DAC-capable pin indices (0xe/0xf) -- the documented 'shared ADC/DAC pin' safety step analogRead() performs before sampling, not DAC output control; then ADC channel setup (INPUTCTRL.MUXPOS masked 0x1f), a start/RESRDY-poll/RESULT-read sequence, and a resolution-shift adjustment (*DAT_0000d2f4 vs *DAT_0000d2f8) matching analogRead()'s _ADCResolution/_readResolution scaling. This is a sensing (ADC input read) primitive; the DAC peripheral touch is incidental library safety logic, not output control.
